card.name: Operators inside dosing formulas
card.fires_on: Math symbols and variables in written clinical formulas, right before a number is expected. Seen in creatinine clearance, ideal body weight, Calvert and osmolality equations.

modes.label: Operators before a constant
modes.description: A plus, minus, divide or times sign inside a formula, just before a numeric constant.

modes.label: Fraction bar or divider
modes.description: The line or slash that splits numerator from denominator in a clearance or osmolality equation.
modes.example: observed CC in mL/min Maintenance Dose Every 12 Hours = ----------------<<----------->>x calculate loading dose in mg normal CC

modes.label: Variable or number in equation
modes.description: A variable name or digit inside the equation, such as glucose or the start of a decimal.

card.writes: It prepares the model to output a number next, such as a constant or amount.
card.plain: It fires on the math signs inside a dosing or lab formula, where a number comes next.
